subject.title: Surface internal system messages in a distinct UI block instead of normal chat bubbles

question: Should intentionally visible runtime/system-originated rows be hidden by default, rendered as a dedicated diagnostic block, or left as ordinary transcript messages with lighter styling?
rationale: The source has enough provenance and UI seams to implement several behaviors, but choosing hidden versus visible diagnostic semantics affects transcript projection, WebChat/Control UI rendering, TUI parity, and restart-continuation behavior.

options.title: Define Shared Audience Contract
options.body: Choose a core hidden-vs-diagnostic audience model first, then implement Gateway projection and UI/TUI rendering from that contract.

options.title: Hide Runtime Internals
options.body: Treat system/runtime-originated user-role rows as agent-only unless explicitly whitelisted for user-visible diagnostics.

options.title: Style Visible System Rows Only
options.body: Add a distinct visual block for role system rows without changing which runtime messages are visible, accepting the risk that agent-only prompts may still be exposed.

recommendation.title: Define Shared Audience Contract
recommendation.body: Choose a core hidden-vs-diagnostic audience model first, then implement Gateway projection and UI/TUI rendering from that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision primarily affects the display projection and Control UI grouping surfaces where recent history points to this owner signal.
